title: Marvin Gaye, a successful soul singer, was struggling with personal and mental health issues in 1983. Despite his recent comeback and success, he was dealing with heavy drug use, paranoia, and delusions. He believed he was being stalked and threatened, and his mind was playing tricks on him. His father, who had once prophesied greatness for his son, had recently passed away, and Marvin's mental state was further deteriorating. The text provides a detailed account of Marvin's tangled relationship with his father and his last days before his tragic death.
